meta.task: Build a small HTTP JSON API, using only the Python standard library (no third-party dependencies), for consulting a mock database of books. Endpoints: list all books, get one book by id (return 404 if missing), and search books by author. Include unit tests.

result.summary: The sources/ directory is empty, so there are no reference files. I read the official Python http.server documentation, which confirms the API can be built with the standard library alone. The route and schema suggestions at the end are my recommendations, not facts from a source.

findings.claim: HTTPServer (a socketserver.TCPServer subclass) and ThreadingHTTPServer (same, but one thread per request, added in 3.7) both require a RequestHandlerClass. The handler can reach the server through its `server` attribute, which is a way to inject the mock data.

BaseHTTPRequestHandler must be subclassed. A request method X is dispatched to do_X(), so GET needs do_GET(). `self.path` includes the query string, so the handler must split it, e.g. with urllib.parse, to read `?author=`.

Responses are written with send_response, send_header, end_headers and then wfile. wfile is a binary stream, so JSON must be encoded to bytes and sent with Content-Type: application/json and Content-Length. If protocol_version is set to HTTP/1.1, an accurate Content-Length is mandatory. The default is HTTP/1.0.

send_error(code, message, explain) returns an HTML error body by default, because error_content_type defaults to 'text/html'. For a JSON 404, either write the response manually with a JSON body or override error_content_type and error_message_format.

The docs warn that http.server is not recommended for production and only implements basic security checks. send_header does not sanitize its input, so untrusted input such as the author query must never be echoed into headers. The default log_message writes to stderr and can be overridden to quiet the tests.

open_questions: No spec was given for the book schema (suggested: id, title, author, year), the routes (suggested: GET /books, GET /books/<id>, GET /books?author=<name>), or whether author search is case-insensitive or substring. The team must decide.
No Python version was specified. The docs I read were for 3.15.2, and ThreadingHTTPServer needs 3.7 or later.
I did not verify a testing approach in any source. Suggested: unittest with the server on port 0 in a background thread, using urllib.request, plus pure unit tests for the data layer.
The error-response format is undefined, including for a non-integer id and for an author search with no matches (suggest 200 with an empty list).

result.goal: Deliver a stdlib-only Python HTTP JSON API over an in-memory mock book database, with endpoints to list books, get a book by id (404 if missing) and search by author, plus unit tests.
in_scope: Book schema: id (int), title, author, year
In-memory mock data module with a small data-access layer: all(), get(id), search_by_author(name)
GET /books returns a JSON list of all books
GET /books/<id> returns one book, or 404 with a JSON error body if missing
GET /books?author=<name> uses case-insensitive substring matching and returns 200 with a list (empty if no matches)
Non-integer id returns 400 with a JSON error. Unknown routes return 404 with JSON. Non-GET methods return 405 with JSON.
http.server (ThreadingHTTPServer) handler with urllib.parse for the path and query. Mock data is injected via the server attribute.
JSON responses use Content-Type: application/json and an accurate Content-Length. Errors are written manually as JSON, not with send_error.
Handler overrides log_message to keep test output quiet
unittest tests: pure data-layer tests, plus integration tests with the server on port 0 in a background thread using urllib.request
Short README with run and test instructions (python -m unittest)
out_of_scope: Authentication, TLS, rate limiting, production hardening
milestones: 1. Fix decisions: routes, schema, search semantics, error format. Set up the project layout (books/data.py, books/server.py, tests/).
2. Implement the mock data and data-access layer, with unit tests.
3. Implement the HTTP handler and server entry point (list, get by id with 404/400, author search, JSON errors).
4. Write integration tests: list, get existing, get missing (404), bad id (400), author match, case-insensitive and substring match, no match, unknown route, wrong method, Content-Type header.
5. Run the full suite and manually smoke-test with curl. Write the README. Confirm no non-stdlib imports.
risks: The spec is silent on schema, routes and search semantics. The chosen defaults may differ from what the requester expects, so they are documented.
Tests that start a real server may be flaky if ports or threads are not cleaned up. Mitigate with port 0, shutdown and server_close in tearDown.
With HTTP/1.1 keep-alive, a wrong Content-Length can hang a client. Mitigate by always encoding the body first and computing its length.
http.server is not production-grade. This is acceptable for a mock API but should be noted in the README.
Untrusted query input must not be echoed into headers. Only JSON bodies are used.
assumptions: Read-only API; the data is a static in-memory list of about 5-10 books
Author search is case-insensitive substring matching, and a search with no matches returns 200 with []
A query string on /books/<id> is ignored
Server binds to 127.0.0.1 on a configurable port

result.design:
# Book API: technical spec

Uses only the Python 3.7+ standard library. Read-only HTTP JSON API over an in-memory mock book database.

## Layout
```
books/__init__.py      package marker (docstring only, no imports)
books/data.py          mock dataset + BookRepository (data-access layer)
books/server.py        HTTP handler, server factory, CLI main()
books/__main__.py      `python3 -m books` entry point -> books.server.main()
tests/__init__.py      empty (enables discovery from the repo root)
tests/test_data.py     pure data-layer tests
tests/test_server.py   integration tests (real server on port 0)
tests/test_project.py  stdlib-only import check + README content check
README.md
```
There are no requirements.txt, setup.py or pyproject files. Allowed imports: json, http.server, urllib.parse, urllib.request, urllib.error, argparse, threading, unittest, contextlib, io, os, sys, re, ast, pathlib, typing, plus the local packages `books` and `tests`.

## Data model (books/data.py)
Each book is a dict with exactly these keys: `{"id": int, "title": str, "author": str, "year": int}`.
`BOOKS` is a module-level list with exactly these 6 entries, in this order (the tests rely on them):
1. The Hobbit, J.R.R. Tolkien, 1937
2. The Fellowship of the Ring, J.R.R. Tolkien, 1954
3. Pride and Prejudice, Jane Austen, 1813
4. Emma, Jane Austen, 1815
5. Nineteen Eighty-Four, George Orwell, 1949
6. Dune, Frank Herbert, 1965

`class BookRepository`:
- `__init__(self, books=None)`: stores shallow copies of each dict from `books`, or from `BOOKS` if `books` is None.
- `all(self) -> list[dict]`: copies of every book, in dataset order.
- `get(self, book_id) -> dict | None`: returns a copy of the book with that id. Returns None if the id is missing or if `book_id` is not an int (bool also counts as not an int).
- `search_by_author(self, name: str) -> list[dict]`: copies of the books where `name.casefold() in book["author"].casefold()`, in dataset order. Returns [] if nothing matches. An empty string matches every book.

Module-level convenience functions `all()`, `get(book_id)` and `search_by_author(name)` delegate to the module-level `DEFAULT_REPOSITORY = BookRepository()`. They are defined with `def` at module level, so `all` intentionally shadows the builtin only inside this module.

## HTTP layer (books/server.py)
- `JSON_CONTENT_TYPE = "application/json"`
- `class BookRequestHandler(http.server.BaseHTTPRequestHandler)`:
  - `protocol_version` stays at the default "HTTP/1.0", so each request gets its own connection and unread request bodies cannot cause keep-alive problems.
  - `_send_json(self, status: int, payload, extra_headers=None)`: `body = json.dumps(payload).encode("utf-8")`. Then it calls send_response(status), sets `Content-Type: application/json` and `Content-Length: len(body)`, adds any extra_headers, calls end_headers(), and writes the body. It skips the body when `self.command == "HEAD"`. This is the only place that writes responses.
  - `send_error(self, code, message=None, explain=None)` is overridden to call `_send_json(code, {"error": message or <default reason phrase for code>})`. As a result, framework-level errors (malformed request line, 501, etc.) are also JSON, never HTML. Handler code itself never calls send_error and instead calls `_send_json` directly.
  - `log_message(self, format, *args)` is overridden as a no-op, so nothing is logged to stderr.
  - `do_GET` does the routing:
    1. `parts = urllib.parse.urlsplit(self.path)`. `path = parts.path`. If path is longer than "/" and ends in "/", one trailing "/" is stripped.
    2. `path == "/books"`: `qs = urllib.parse.parse_qs(parts.query, keep_blank_values=True)`. If "author" is in qs, return 200 with `repo.search_by_author(qs["author"][0])`. Otherwise return 200 with `repo.all()`. Other query parameters are ignored.
    3. If path matches `^/books/([^/]+)$`: `seg = urllib.parse.unquote(group1)`. If seg does not fully match `[0-9]+` (ASCII digits only), return 400 `{"error": "invalid book id"}`. Otherwise `book = repo.get(int(seg))`, and return 200 with the book, or 404 `{"error": "book not found"}` if it is None. The query string is ignored on this route.
    4. Anything else returns 404 `{"error": "not found"}`.
    - `repo = self.server.repository`. The data is injected through the server attribute.
  - `do_POST`, `do_PUT`, `do_DELETE`, `do_PATCH`, `do_HEAD` and `do_OPTIONS` all return 405 `{"error": "method not allowed"}` with the extra header `Allow: GET`.
  - Error messages are fixed strings. User input is never echoed into headers or error bodies.
- `create_server(host="127.0.0.1", port=8000, repository=None) -> http.server.ThreadingHTTPServer`: builds the server with BookRequestHandler, sets `server.repository = repository or BookRepository()` and `server.daemon_threads = True`, and returns it without starting it. The actual port is `server.server_address[1]`, which matters when port 0 is used.
- `parse_args(argv=None) -> argparse.Namespace`: `--host` (default "127.0.0.1") and `--port` (int, default 8000).
- `main(argv=None) -> None`: parses the arguments, calls create_server, prints `Serving on http://{host}:{port}` to stdout, and runs serve_forever. On KeyboardInterrupt it exits; in all cases it calls server_close in a `finally` block.
- `books/__main__.py`: `from books.server import main` followed by `if __name__ == "__main__": main()`.

## Responses summary
| Request | Status | Body |
|---|---|---|
| GET /books | 200 | list of all books |
| GET /books?author=x | 200 | list of matches (case-insensitive substring), possibly [] |
| GET /books/<digits> existing | 200 | book object |
| GET /books/<digits> missing | 404 | {"error": "book not found"} |
| GET /books/<non-digits> | 400 | {"error": "invalid book id"} |
| GET other path | 404 | {"error": "not found"} |
| POST/PUT/DELETE/PATCH/HEAD/OPTIONS on any path | 405 | {"error": "method not allowed"} (no body for HEAD) |

Every response has `Content-Type: application/json` and an exact Content-Length.

## Testing approach
- `tests/test_data.py`: tests BookRepository and the module-level functions directly.
- `tests/test_server.py`: `setUpClass` calls `create_server(port=0)`, starts `serve_forever` in a daemon `threading.Thread`, and builds base_url from server_address. `tearDownClass` calls `server.shutdown()`, `server.server_close()` and `thread.join(timeout=5)`. The helper `request(method, path)` uses urllib.request, catches `urllib.error.HTTPError` and returns `(status, headers, raw_body_bytes)`. The suite has a separate test class with its own server that uses an injected custom BookRepository, to prove data comes from `self.server.repository`.
- `tests/test_project.py`: AST-scans every .py file under books/ and tests/ and checks that all imports are in the allow-list. Also checks that the README contents are present.
- Command: `python3 -m unittest -v` from the repo root.

I built work item W1: the mock book dataset, the data-access layer and its unit tests. All 17 tests pass.

Files:
- **`books/__init__.py`**: a docstring only.
- **`tests/__init__.py`**: empty.
- **`books/data.py`**: no imports.
  - `BOOKS`: the 6 books from the design, ids 1–6, in the specified order.
  - `BookRepository`: copies the books it's given when created (the built-in dataset if none are given) and stores those copies. `all()`, `get()` and `search_by_author()` all return copies in dataset order.
    - `get()` returns `None` for a missing id, and also for any id that isn't an int, including `True`/`False`.
    - `search_by_author()` matches any part of the author name, ignoring case. An empty name matches every book.
  - `DEFAULT_REPOSITORY`, plus module-level `all()`, `get()` and `search_by_author()` that call it.
- **`tests/test_data.py`**: covers everything the work item lists:
  - The dataset has 5–10 books, each with exactly the four keys and the right types (an id can't be a bool), and the ids are unique.
  - `all()` equals `BOOKS` in order.
  - `get()`: id 1 returns The Hobbit; 99999, `'1'` and `True` return `None`.
  - Search: `'J.R.R. Tolkien'`, `'TOLK'` and `'tolk'` each return books [1, 2]; `'austen'` returns [3, 4]; `'nobody'` returns []; `''` returns all books.
  - Changing a returned book doesn't affect later results.
  - A repository built from custom books uses only those books.
  - The module-level functions return the same results as `DEFAULT_REPOSITORY`.

I added three small tests beyond the list: a repository keeps its own copy of the books it's given, an empty repository returns nothing, and `get()` also rejects `1.0` and `None`.

result.summary:
I built the HTTP server (`books/server.py`), the `python3 -m books` entry point (`books/__main__.py`) and the integration tests (`tests/test_server.py`), following the design. The full suite passes: 39 tests, including the 13 data-layer tests from W1.

**`books/server.py`**
- **One response writer:** every response goes through `_send_json`. It encodes the JSON body first, then sets `Content-Type: application/json` and an exact `Content-Length`, and sends no body for HEAD requests.
- **Errors:** `send_error` is overridden, so errors raised by `http.server` itself (such as 501 for an unknown method) also come back as `{"error": ...}` instead of HTML. Our own code never calls `send_error`.
- **No logging:** `log_message` does nothing, so nothing is written to stderr.
- **Routing in `do_GET`:** paths and queries are parsed with `urllib.parse`, and one trailing slash is ignored.
  - `/books` returns all books, or matching books when `?author=` is given.
  - `/books/<digits>` returns the book, or 404 if it doesn't exist.
  - An id that isn't plain digits (e.g. `abc`, `-1`) gets 400.
  - Any other path gets 404.
  - Data is read only from `self.server.repository`.
- **Other methods:** POST, PUT, DELETE, PATCH, HEAD and OPTIONS all get 405 with `Allow: GET`. Error messages are fixed strings and never include anything from the request.
- **Startup:** `create_server()` defaults to 127.0.0.1, attaches the repository and sets `daemon_threads=True`. `parse_args()` handles `--host`/`--port`. `main()` prints `Serving on http://host:port`, runs the server, stops quietly on Ctrl+C and always closes the server.

**Choices beyond the spec**
- **Very long ids:** an id made of more digits than Python will convert to an integer now gets 404 instead of causing a server-side traceback.
- **Request bodies on 405:** for 405 responses, the server reads any request body up to 64 KB before replying. Without this, the client can see a connection reset.
- **Repository check:** `create_server` uses `repository if repository is not None` instead of `repository or ...`, so an injected repository is never replaced with the default dataset.

**`tests/test_server.py`** covers every case listed in the work item. It also tests:
- PATCH, OPTIONS and HEAD returning 405 (HEAD with an empty body);
- an unknown method (`BREW`) getting a JSON 501;
- the very-long-id 404 and `/books/1.5` getting 400;
- `main()` printing its address and closing the server on Ctrl+C;
- no non-daemon threads left running, checked both as a test and in `tearDownModule`.

That is 13 tests from `tests/test_data.py` and 26 from `tests/test_server.py`. They covered listing books, the trailing slash, getting by id with and without a query string, 404/400/405 responses, author search, the Content-Type and Content-Length checks, the CR/LF header-injection request, empty stderr, the injected repository, the server factory, `parse_args`, `main()` and leftover threads.

I also ran a manual check of the entry point: `python3 -m books --port 8765` printed `Serving on http://127.0.0.1:8765`, GET `/books/6` returned the Dune book as JSON, and nothing was written to stderr.

item.title: HTTP handler, server factory, CLI entry point and integration tests
item.description: Implement books/server.py exactly as in the design: BookRequestHandler with _send_json as the single response writer (json body encoded first, Content-Type application/json, exact Content-Length, no body for HEAD); a send_error override that emits JSON {"error": ...}; a no-op log_message; do_GET routing via urllib.parse.urlsplit/parse_qs/unquote (/books, /books?author=, /books/<[0-9]+>, 400 for non-digit ids, 404 for missing books and unknown paths, trailing slash tolerated); 405 JSON with Allow: GET for POST/PUT/DELETE/PATCH/HEAD/OPTIONS; data read only from self.server.repository; fixed error strings with no user input echoed. Also implement create_server(host='127.0.0.1', port=8000, repository=None) returning a ThreadingHTTPServer with .repository and daemon_threads=True, parse_args(argv), and main(argv) (prints 'Serving on http://host:port', serve_forever, server_close in finally, exits cleanly on KeyboardInterrupt). Create books/__main__.py, which calls main(). tests/test_server.py (unittest + urllib.request, server on port 0 in a background thread, shutdown/server_close/join in tearDownClass) must test: GET /books returns 200 with the full BOOKS list; /books/ with a trailing slash behaves the same; /books/1 returns 200 with book 1; /books/1?x=y is the same; /books/99999 returns 404 with an 'error' key; /books/abc and /books/-1 return 400 with an 'error' key; author=J.R.R.%20Tolkien, author=TOLKIEN and author=olk each return books [1, 2]; author=zzz returns 200 with []; GET /nope and /books/1/extra return 404 JSON; POST (with a small body), PUT and DELETE to /books each return 405 JSON with Allow: GET; for success, 400, 404 and 405 responses, Content-Type == 'application/json', int(Content-Length) == len(body), and the body does not start with '<'; GET /books?author=%0D%0AX-Injected:%20yes returns 200 [] and has no X-Injected header; requests made under contextlib.redirect_stderr(io.StringIO()) leave the captured stderr empty; a second test class whose server uses an injected BookRepository with one custom book gets exactly that book from /books; create_server(port=0).server_address[0] == '127.0.0.1'; parse_args(['--port','9001']).port == 9001 with default host 127.0.0.1; and every test run leaves no non-daemon threads running.

item.title: README and project-level checks (stdlib-only, docs)
item.description: Write README.md with: a project summary; requirements (Python 3.7+, stdlib only, no dependencies); the run command `python3 -m books --port 8000` (with --host, default 127.0.0.1); the test command `python -m unittest` (and `python3 -m unittest -v`); the three endpoints GET /books, GET /books/<id> and GET /books?author=<name> with example curl commands and example responses; the book schema (id int, title str, author str, year int); search semantics (case-insensitive substring, no matches gives 200 []); the error format {"error": ...} with the 400/404/405 cases; and a note that http.server is not production-grade and is only meant for this mock API. Write tests/test_project.py (unittest): (1) uses ast to parse every .py file under books/ and tests/ and asserts that every Import/ImportFrom top-level module (ignoring relative imports) is in the allow-list {json, http, urllib, argparse, threading, unittest, contextlib, io, os, sys, re, ast, pathlib, typing, books, tests}; (2) asserts that requirements.txt, setup.py, Pipfile and pyproject.toml do not exist at the repo root; (3) asserts that README.md exists and contains 'python -m unittest', 'python3 -m books', '/books/<id>', '/books?author=' and the phrase 'not production-grade'. Resolve paths relative to the repo root via pathlib.Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent.
